name: Motor stator temperature
why: derate before the magnets are damaged; the thermal limit is what actually caps a long run, not the peak torque number
calibration: ice bath + boiling water, 2-point, before each event

name: Inverter / IGBT temperature
why: the inverter derates on this; logging it explains torque loss that otherwise looks like a driver or a grip problem
calibration: cross-check the broadcast value against a surface probe on the heatsink during a cool-down

name: Coolant temperature — radiator inlet
why: with the outlet probe and the flow meter, gives measured heat rejection instead of a spreadsheet estimate
calibration: 2-point against a reference RTD at 20 C and 60 C

name: Coolant temperature — radiator outlet
why: the other half of the delta-T that sizes the radiator
calibration: 2-point against a reference RTD at 20 C and 60 C

name: Coolant flow rate
why: turns the delta-T into kilowatts; without it the temperature pair measures a difference of unknown significance
calibration: gravimetric, 3 flow points, bucket and scale

name: Damper position, front left
why: damper velocity histogram; sets the low-speed knee we actually run at Michigan
calibration: dial gauge against the pot at 10 mm steps, both directions, check hysteresis

name: Steering angle
why: separates driver input from yaw response when a corner goes wrong on the data
calibration: centre with the rack at mid-travel, then lock-to-lock against a protractor on the hub

name: Wheel speed FL
why: slip ratio for the traction controller, and the only honest check that a corner locked under braking
calibration: rolling road at three known speeds; confirm the tooth count in firmware matches the ring

name: Wheel speed FR
why: slip ratio for the traction controller, and the only honest check that a corner locked under braking
calibration: rolling road at three known speeds; confirm the tooth count in firmware matches the ring

name: Wheel speed RL
why: slip ratio for the traction controller, and the only honest check that a corner locked under braking
calibration: rolling road at three known speeds; confirm the tooth count in firmware matches the ring

name: Wheel speed RR
why: slip ratio for the traction controller, and the only honest check that a corner locked under braking
calibration: rolling road at three known speeds; confirm the tooth count in firmware matches the ring

name: Brake pressure, front circuit
why: proves brake balance and gives the rules a trace showing all four wheels locked

name: Tractive system current
why: energy used per lap, and the number the endurance strategy is actually built on
calibration: against a clamp meter at 10 A, 50 A and 150 A with the car on jacks

name: GNSS position
why: lap segmentation, so every other channel can be compared corner by corner instead of by eye
calibration: static soak on a surveyed point for 10 min; check the reported fix type is RTK before trusting the trace
